about: The Caffo story begins on the slopes of Mount Etna, where Giuseppe Caffo worked as a master distiller of grape pomace in the late 1800s. In 1915 he bought a distillery of his own in Santa Venerina, near Catania. His son Sebastiano and his brothers, back from years in Australia, later revived an old distillery across the Strait in Limbadi, Calabria, which became the heart of the company, best known for Vecchio Amaro del Capo. The family still runs it, led by Sebastiano “Nuccio” Caffo and the founder’s grandson and namesake, Giuseppe.

Many amarettos get their flavour from crushed apricot kernels. Caffo’s is made with almonds, hand-picked in Sicily, which its importer says come from the family’s own estate. They are infused with aromatic herbs and vanilla, and the liqueur is built on a neutral grain spirit with aged brandy added before bottling at 30% alcohol. The label carries the title Fratelli d’Italia, “Brothers of Italy,” a dedication to the Italian emigrants for whom it was created.

Its importer’s tasting note finds almond first, with a hint of black cherry and the warm baking spices of Italian confectionery. The emigrant dedication fits a family whose second generation spent years working in Australia. It belongs at the end of the meal: poured neat or over ice, served beside an espresso, or stirred into an Amaretto Sour.
facts: Neutral grain spirit, with aged brandy
Sicilian almonds (no apricot kernels), herbs and vanilla
title: Caffo Amaretto
